documents: Wang & Wei 2022, J Metamorph Geol 40:1529-1544, published PDF

entry.evidence: Therefore, there are still some unreconciled discrepancies between thermodynamic calculations and experimental constraints on phase equilibria in UHT metapelites, especially in oxidized conditions.

steps.action: Take from the literature the experimentally determined FMASO reaction clusters (R1-R3 reduced, R4-R5 oxidized) of Hensen (1986) and Hensen & Green (1973).
steps.quote: have determined that the crucial metamorphic reactions R1 (Opx + Sil = Spr + Grt)

steps.action: Set previously calculated KFMASHTO projections and pseudosections (Wheller & Powell 2014; Korhonen et al. 2012) against experiments: topologies diverge and Spr-Qz is stable below 900 °C, whereas Das et al. experiments need >1000 °C.
steps.quote: distinctly diverge from the experimental results in Figure 1b

steps.action: State the unresolved mismatch between thermodynamic calculations and experiments for oxidized UHT metapelites.
steps.quote: there are still some unreconciled discrepancies between thermodynamic calculations and experimental constraints

steps.action: Point to ferric sillimanite in high-fO2 UHT rocks as an unmodelled ingredient that may explain the mismatch, against the received attribution to fO2 alone.
steps.quote: [...] with high fO2 were reported to contain sillimanite with considerable Fe2O3 contents

steps.action: Compile bulk-rock compositions of UHT metapelites worldwide and divide them into HMg, LMgHO and LMgLO types (Figure 2).
steps.quote: UHT metapelites that contain the diagnostic assemblages of Spr–Qz and/or Opx–Sil have two distinct types of bulk compositions

steps.action: Fix the aim: the effect of Fe2O3 in sillimanite on phase equilibria in the three types of UHT metapelites.
steps.quote: the aim of this study is to investigate the effects of Fe2O3 in sillimanite on phase equilibria

steps.action: Compile published Fe2O3 contents of sillimanite by rock type and metamorphic grade (Figure 3) and show that Fe2O3 increases with grade.
steps.quote: which implies that Fe2O3 in sillimanite (Fe2O3[Sil]) increases with higher metamorphic grades

steps.action: Construct a Fe3+-Al(VI) sill-fsill activity model (symmetric formalism, W = 1 kJ, fictive endmember with ΔG_make = 29 kJ taken from the authors' Wang et al. 2020, via Hess's law and oxide sums).
steps.quote: a value of the macroscopic interaction energy W(sill, fsill) = 1 kJ is adopted

steps.action: Test the model by calculating a KFMASHO P-T pseudosection for the experimental starting material M1 of Das et al. and comparing it with the synthetic assemblages (Figure 4a).
steps.quote: In order to test the activity model of ferric sillimanite established above, we calculated a P–T pseudosection

steps.action: Analyse the sensitivity to ΔG_make with a T-ΔG pseudosection at 10 kbar; only 28-31 kJ reproduces the experimental parageneses.
steps.quote: the sensitivity of the calculated results to the estimated value of

steps.action: Compare calculated Fe2O3 in sillimanite against temperature with compiled natural and experimental data (Figure 4c).
steps.quote: is in reasonable agreement with the statistical results from natural and experimental samples

steps.action: Calculate P-T projections in KFMASH, KFMASHO and KFMASHTO with pure versus ferric sillimanite, with Ilm-Rt or Ilm-Mag in excess for low or high fO2 (Figure 5).
steps.quote: Sillimanite is set to be pure versus ferric for comparison.

steps.action: Compare the ferric-sillimanite KFMASHTO projection (Figure 5e) with the experimentally calibrated projection (Figure 1b): R1-R5 match and R1 is shifted 60-80 °C higher.
steps.quote: especially the crucial reactions R1 to R5, can match those

steps.action: Calculate P-T and T-XFe3+ pseudosections, pure versus ferric sillimanite, for three representative samples (Jining LMgHO, Napier HMg, Kerala LMgLO), beginning with Jining (Figures 6, 7).
steps.quote: Three different types of representative UHT metapelite samples were selected

steps.action: Compare the Jining ferric-sillimanite pseudosection (R1, R2, Opx-Sil, Spr-Grt, Spr-Spl) with experimental constraints; sapphirine is raised 60-70 °C.
steps.quote: are in good agreement with the experimentally constrained results from Hensen (1986) and Das et al. (2001, 2003)

steps.action: Extend the comparison to the HMg Napier and LMgLO Kerala compositions: R1 is consistent with experiments for Napier, the ferric effect is small (≤20-40 °C), and no R1-R3 occurs for Kerala in P-T.
steps.quote: consistent with the experimental results (e.g., Hensen & Green, 1973)

steps.action: Calculate AFM compatibility diagrams along an 8 kbar isobaric heating path with ferric sillimanite and plot the three sample types (Figure 10).
steps.quote: A series of AFM compatibility diagrams

steps.action: Keep the claim that ferric sillimanite reconciles calculations with experiments and raises R1 by up to ~40 °C (high-MgO) and ~60 °C (low-MgO).
steps.quote: This improved the reconciliation of thermodynamic calculations with petrological experiments.

steps.action: Restrict the Fe2O3(Sil) thermometer to high-fO2 fields (XFe3+ > 0.45) and state that the ferric effect is negligible in HMg and LMgLO rocks.
steps.quote: the Fe2O3(Sil) isopleths can indicate temperatures only in the high-fO2 fields

steps.action: Check the predicted reaction control against published natural oxidized Spr-bearing granulites (Wilson Lake, Daqingshan), which are also governed by R1 and R2.
steps.quote: are also governed by R1 and R2 (Jiao et al., 2015; Korhonen et al., 2012)

steps.action: Explain the mismatch between the projection-predicted R1 (~1040 °C) and the pseudosection R1 (~980-1000 °C) by CaO-extended garnet stability, rather than revising the model.
steps.quote: This may result from the stability expansion of Garnet by the incorporation of CaO

steps.action: Keep the petrogenetic framework: low-fO2 reactions R1-R3 prevail, with R1 and R2 the most common in UHT metapelites and Grt-Sil persisting in LMgLO rocks.
steps.quote: R1 and R2 are the most common reactions that work in UHT metapelites

end.claim: Incorporating Fe3+ into sillimanite largely resolves the topological mismatch between thermodynamic calculations and experiments at high fO2 and raises the temperature switching Opx+Sil to Spr+Qz by about 50-70 °C in oxidized metapelites.

decisive_move.sentence: Constructing the ferric sillimanite activity model (Table 1) is what allows the pure-versus-ferric comparison; without it no shifted equilibria could be calculated.

gates.evidence: No new data were acquired, but the hypothesis that ferric sillimanite matters directed which calculations were run (pure versus ferric, p. 1534). The model could have failed to match the Das et al. M1 experiments and the Figure 1b topology (pp. 1532-1536). However, ΔG_make was bounded with the same experiments (28-31 kJ, p. 1534). ΔG_make = 29 kJ was fixed earlier, in Wang et al. 2020, before this test.

imports.item: Hess's law to derive the fictive-endmember enthalpy adjustment
Ionic radii of Al3+ and low-spin Fe3+ to justify octahedral substitution
Calorimetric enthalpies for ferric corundum (Majzlan et al. 2002) and the quartz-corundum combination (Charlu et al. 1975)

novelty_claims.quote: These differences have not yet been the subject of detailed study.

limits: No review file was supplied; the acknowledgements (p. 1541) mention an editor and two reviewers, but no review sequence can be coded. No new samples or experiments; all experimental and natural data are cited. ΔG_make comes from the authors' earlier work (Wang et al. 2020). The M1 experiments serve both to bound ΔG_make and to test the model, so the test is partly calibration (inference). Composition none_fits: the walk is model construction followed by comparison of two model variants against cited experiments, with no decisive exclusion of a rival. Sub-claims and their statuses: the Fe2O3(Sil) thermometer is regularity_in_range, valid only at XFe3+ > 0.45 (p. 1541); the R1-R2 petrogenetic framework is best_explanation (p. 1541); the CaO explanation for the offset in R1 temperature is speculative ('may result', p. 1541). The paper reports no uncertainty propagation on the calculated reaction temperatures.

disagreements.target: Wheller and Powell (2014) calculated KFMASHTO P-T projection
disagreements.support: The ferric-sillimanite projection (Figure 5e) reproduces the experimental topology (Figure 1b), which the pure-sillimanite projection does not.
disagreements.quote: distinctly diverge from the experimental results in Figure 1b

disagreements.target: Calculated pseudosections for high-fO2 UHT metapelites (Korhonen et al. 2012; Li & Wei 2018; Taylor-Jones & Powell 2010)
disagreements.support: With ferric sillimanite, sapphirine and R1 move 40-70 °C higher, closer to the >1000 °C limit from the Das et al. experiments.
disagreements.quote: [...] -bearing mineral assemblages were stabilized to much lower temperatures than that in low-fO2 metapelites

disagreements.target: Community attribution of Spr-Qz stability expansion solely to high fO2
disagreements.support: Fe3+ partitioning into sillimanite deprives sapphirine of Fe3+ and raises R1, so fO2 is not the only control.
disagreements.quote: Such stability expansion of the Spr–Qz assemblage has been solely attributed to the high fO2 of the rocks until now.

disagreements.target: Distinguishing fO2 by excess Ilm-Rt versus Ilm-Mag (Wheller & Powell 2014)
disagreements.support: The T-XFe3+ pseudosections show that magnetite is absent in the Napier composition, so the distinction works only roughly, in low-MgO rocks.
disagreements.quote: the distinction of oxygen fugacity by excess Ilm–Rt and Ilm–Mag may work roughly in low-MgO rocks

alternatives_considered.reason: to avoid a variance increase of Spl-Mag-involved reactions
